_note: Watch DBF — original Delaware Beach Finds video. Every `src` is a first-party clip shot by DBF, transcoded from the master library to H.264 for the web. Masters live outside the repo and are never modified. An entry renders only when it has BOTH a local `src` and a local `poster`; never point `src` at Instagram or any third-party host.
_pipeline: scripts/add_watch_clip.py turns an approved master into a web derivative, a poster and a manifest entry. See automation/VIDEO_ASSET_REQUIREMENTS.md.

entries.title: Driving the beach past a fire-control tower
entries.context: There is a stretch of Delaware beach you can drive, and a WWII fire-control tower standing right off the sand. Most people pass it without knowing what it is.
entries.posterAlt: A concrete fire-control tower standing beyond the sand, seen from a truck driving on the beach
entries.relatedLabel: Read: What the Dunes Were For

entries.title: The Bandstand at dusk
entries.context: Rehoboth's boardwalk in the last of the light — the bandstand, the bikes, and the shopfronts everybody photographs without meaning to.
entries.posterAlt: The Rehoboth Beach bandstand at dusk with people walking the boardwalk

entries.title: A channel through the marsh
entries.context: The tidal creeks behind the dunes are where most of the bay's life actually starts. Quiet, green, and moving faster than it looks.
entries.posterAlt: A tidal channel winding through green Delaware marsh

entries.title: Surf on an empty beach
entries.context: No umbrellas, no crowd — just the Atlantic doing what it does when nobody is scheduled to be there.
entries.posterAlt: Waves breaking on an empty Delaware beach

entries.title: Boardwalk, mid-afternoon
entries.context: The working end of the boardwalk: shopfronts, foot traffic, and the particular light that comes off wet planks.
entries.posterAlt: Shopfronts and people along the Rehoboth Beach boardwalk
entries.relatedLabel: Read: What the Boardwalk Smells Like in July

entries.title: The long view down the sand
entries.context: Looking down the beach with the surf running in from the left. This is most of what a Delaware beach day actually looks like.
entries.posterAlt: A long stretch of Delaware beach with surf breaking

entries.title: The turbine over the marsh
entries.context: Not every Delaware landmark is old. The turbine is visible from a long way off across the wetland.
entries.posterAlt: A wind turbine standing beyond Delaware marshland
entries.relatedLabel: Read: Where the Marsh Is Going

entries.title: A Wednesday at the beach
entries.context: Midweek, off season hours, nobody around. Filed under: reasons to live here.
entries.posterAlt: Small waves running onto empty Delaware sand
